name: baak ging haau aap
aliases: baak ging haau aap, běi jīng kǎo yā, 北京烤鸭
description: A dish of duck with crispy roasted skin, famous for it's origin from Peking (modern Beijing).
originalName: baak ging haau aap, běi jīng kǎo yā, 北京烤鸭

name: Bak cheet gai
aliases: Bak cheet gai, bái qì jī, 白切雞
description: "White steamed chicken" is a whole chicken salted and steamed until cooked, and served chopped (bone in). It is typically accompanied by a dish of minced ginger, scallions, and salt suspended in oil.
originalName: Bak cheet gai, bái qì jī, 白切雞

name: Bak cheurk Ha
aliases: Bak cheurk Ha, bái zhuó há, 白灼蝦
description: A simple way to have shrimp in cantonese restaurants; this is basically blanched shrimp which can be dipped in soy sauce seasoned with chilli peppers.
originalName: Bak cheurk Ha, bái zhuó há, 白灼蝦

name: bo chai faan
aliases: bo chai faan, bào zǐ fàn, 煲仔飯
description: A class of various dishes where slow cooked ingredients are served over rice and vegetables in a scalding hot clay pot.
originalName: bo chai faan, bào zǐ fàn, 煲仔飯

name: Bok Choy
description: Related to Cabbage and turnip, bok choy is a common vegetable in chinese cooking. Its main nutritional benefit is vitamin C.

name: Cha chee gai
aliases: Cha chee gai, zhà zǐ jī, 炸子雞
description: Whole chicken roasted until skin is crispy, served chopped with bone in, typically with a blend of spiced salt.
originalName: Cha chee gai, zhà zǐ jī, 炸子雞

name: Cha Leung
aliases: Cha Leung, zhà liǎng, 炸兩
summary: Fried Dough wrapped with rice crepe
description: Dish of fried dough wrapped with rice crepe, drizzled with sweetened soy sauce.
originalName: Cha Leung, zhà liǎng, 炸兩

name: Cha siu
aliases: Cha siu, cha shao, 叉烧
description: Sweet Marinated pork loin, roasted or loosely "barbequed"
originalName: Cha siu, cha shao, 叉烧

name: Cha Sui Bow
aliases: Cha Sui Bow, cha shao bāo, 叉烧包
summary: Barbeque pork buns, steamed or baked, Dim Sum
description: Barbeque pork buns, steamed or baked
originalName: Cha Sui Bow, cha shao bāo, 叉烧包

name: Cha Yeep Dan
aliases: Cha Yeep Dan, chá yè dàn, 茶葉蛋
summary: Hard Boiled eggs cooked in tea .
originalName: Cha Yeep Dan, chá yè dàn, 茶葉蛋

name: chao fahn
aliases: chao fahn, chao fàn, 炒饭
originalName: chao fahn, chao fàn, 炒饭

name: chǎo mien
aliases: chǎo mien, chǎo miǎn, 炒面
summary: Stir or deep fried Fried Noodles
description: Stir Fried Noodles of the wheat and/or egg based variety (as opposed to rice noodles). Can be made with many ingredients and different types of noodle depending on region of specialty. Hong Kong Style would have ingredients served over a deep fried cake of crispy noodles. Other Chinese styles would have the noodles stir fried with ingredients with little sauce and with thicker more flour consistency noodles.
originalName: chǎo mien, chǎo miǎn, 炒面

name: chǎo
summary: To Stir Fry, traditionally, in a wok

name: Char Sui Sou
aliases: Char Sui Sou, cha shāo sū, 叉烧 酥
summary: Flaky Pastry filled with barbeque pork (cha shui)
originalName: Char Sui Sou, cha shāo sū, 叉烧 酥

name: Cheung Fun
aliases: Cheung Fun, cháng fěn, 腸粉
summary: Savory rice crepes, Dim Sum dish
description: Savory rice crepes wrapped around meats like cha sui, shrimp (ha), or minced beef, then served with a drizzle of sweetened soy sauce
originalName: Cheung Fun, cháng fěn, 腸粉

name: Chien chang go
aliases: Chien chang go, qiān céng gāo, 千層糕
description: A sweet cake of mung bean paste, sweetened and blended with salted egg (Haam Daan 鹹蛋), layered over fluffy white bread (similar to the dough in cha sui bow 叉烧包).
originalName: Chien chang go, qiān céng gāo, 千層糕

name: Ching Sui Dan
aliases: Ching Sui Dan, zhēng shuǐ dàn, 蒸水蛋
description: A savory dish of eggs, blended with water to make a soft custard, often steamed with various ingredients to add flavor. Common additions may be dried scallops, pork, or pickled vegetables.
originalName: Ching Sui Dan, zhēng shuǐ dàn, 蒸水蛋

name: chiu-chau fun guo
aliases: chiu-chau fun guo, cháo zhōu fěn guǒ, 潮州粉果
summary: Dumpling of pork, peanuts, dried shrimp, and mushrooms
description: Dim Sum: A dumpling made of pork peanuts, chives, dried shrimp, and mushrooms. The wrapping is rice flour and thick but translucent
originalName: chiu-chau fun guo, cháo zhōu fěn guǒ, 潮州粉果

name: Chong Yow Beng
aliases: Chong Yow Beng, cong you bing, 葱油饼
originalName: Chong Yow Beng, cong you bing, 葱油饼

name: chou dou fu
aliases: chou dou fu, chòu dòu fǔ, 臭豆腐
originalName: chou dou fu, chòu dòu fǔ, 臭豆腐

name: Chow Mein
aliases: Chow Mein, chǎo miàn, 炒麵
description: Stir Fried Noodles 炒麵 can be made with all kinds of ingredients but cooking styles vary from different regions. Hong Kong Style chow mein sometimes involves deep fried thin egg noodles with ingredients and sauce poured over.
originalName: Chow Mein, chǎo miàn, 炒麵

name: Choy sum
aliases: Choy sum, cài xīn, 菜心
description: "vegetable heart", choy sum refers to the delicate tender shoots of bok choy, which is a common vegetable related to cabbage.
originalName: Choy sum, cài xīn, 菜心

name: Chuen Guen
aliases: Chuen Guen, chūn juǎn, 春捲
description: The classic chinese egg roll is literally called "Spring Roll". A deep fried thin skin is wrapped around various fillings; typically meat and some vegetables. Sometimes a sweet and sour dipping sauce accompanies the dish.
originalName: Chuen Guen, chūn juǎn, 春捲

name: Chun Pei Wu Tau Aap
aliases: Chun Pei Wu Tau Aap, chén pí hū tóu yā, 陳皮芋頭鴨
description: A dish of duck meat, slow steamed soft, mixed with taro, then deep fried into a crispy cake.
originalName: Chun Pei Wu Tau Aap, chén pí hū tóu yā, 陳皮芋頭鴨

name: chung hing lat ji gai
aliases: chung hing lat ji gai, Chóng qìng là zǐ jī, 重庆辣子雞
description: "Heavy heat chili chicken"; a dish of deep fried chicken pieces cooked with copious amounts of chilis; a sichuan dish.
originalName: chung hing lat ji gai, Chóng qìng là zǐ jī, 重庆辣子雞

name: Daan taat
aliases: Daan taat, dàn tà, 蛋撻
description: Sweet Egg Custard baked in a flaky tart base
originalName: Daan taat, dàn tà, 蛋撻

name: Dan Dan Mien
aliases: Dan Dan Mien, Dan Dan miǎn, 担担面
summary: Szechuan dish of flour noodles mixed with hot chili oil, minced pork, spices (including star anice) and peanuts.
description: Szechuan dish of flour noodles mixed with hot chili oil, minced pork, spices (including star anice) and peanuts.
originalName: Dan Dan Mien, Dan Dan miǎn, 担担面

name: Dau fu fa
aliases: Dau fu fa, dòu fǔ huā, 豆腐花
summary: Dessert of soft tofu suspended in sugar water.
originalName: Dau fu fa, dòu fǔ huā, 豆腐花

name: dau fu
aliases: dau fu, dòu fǔ, 豆腐
description: Tofu: literally translated "rotten bean", tofu is produced by coagulating soy milk using a variety of mineral coagulants that produce various textures. Firm tofu is commonly produced with calcium sulfate, softer silk tofu's with Calcium chloride or magnesium chloride. Tofu is thus rich in calcium or magnesium, protein, and low in fat.
originalName: dau fu, dòu fǔ, 豆腐

name: dau jerng
aliases: dau jerng, Dau jiāng, 豆漿
description: Sweet or savory soy soup, usually eaten warm. If savory, it can be flavored with chopped pickled vegetables, dried shrimp, or other seasonings and accompanied with chinese fried bread.
originalName: dau jerng, Dau jiāng, 豆漿

name: Dim sum
aliases: Dim sum, dian xin, 点心
summary: Dishes of small portions with many varieties
description: Literally translated "touching the heart", dims sum are dishes of small portions of many varieties. Some classics are Sui Mai (steamed pork dumpling), Hah Gao (steamed shrimp dumpling), Cha Sui Bow (barbeque pork bun), Cheung Fun (rice drough crepe). Once can consider Dim Sum the original asian Tapas.
originalName: Dim sum, dian xin, 点心

name: dun daan
aliases: dun daan, dùn đản, 燉蛋
description: A dessert of Steamed egg custard in a bowl.
originalName: dun daan, dùn đản, 燉蛋

name: Dun Lai
aliases: Dun Lai, dùn nǎi, 燉奶
description: A dessert of steamed milk, congealed with egg white, and often flavored with various syrups in individual bowls. Commonly this is ginger flavored.
originalName: Dun Lai, dùn nǎi, 燉奶

name: Dungh Gwa Jung
aliases: Dungh Gwa Jung, dōng guā shāng, 冬瓜湯
description: Wintermelon soup is a clear broth flavored often with dried scallops, pork, and the wintermelon (A mild flavored melon with soft white flesh, growing to proportions larger than watermelons). The soup is often served a hollowed out shell of a wintermelon.
originalName: Dungh Gwa Jung, dōng guā shāng, 冬瓜湯

name: faan syu
aliases: faan syu, bō shǔ, 番薯
originalName: faan syu, bō shǔ, 番薯

name: Fo woa
aliases: Fo woa, huǒ guō, 火锅
description: A style of meal where a pot of boiling soup is kept hot on the table while diners cook various ingredients by immersion into the soup. By the end of the meal, a rich broth remains.
originalName: Fo woa, huǒ guō, 火锅

name: fu chai fai pin
aliases: fu chai fai pin, fū qī fèi piàn, 夫妻肺片
description: A dish of spicy organ meats, originating from Chengdu china. "Husband Wife Lung Slices" is made of beef lungs, stomach, intestines, and tongue, heavily spiced and may be served cold. This is a common street dish.
originalName: fu chai fai pin, fū qī fèi piàn, 夫妻肺片

name: Fu Pei Guen
aliases: Fu Pei Guen, fǔ pí juǎn, 腐皮捲
description: A dim sum of tofu skin, which is a soy wrapping, steamed around minced pork mixed with chopped bamboo shoots in a rich sauce.
originalName: Fu Pei Guen, fǔ pí juǎn, 腐皮捲

name: Fu yu
aliases: Fu yu, fǔ rǔ, 腐乳
description: Strong flavored fermented tofu; often spiced and in heavy brine. This can be eaten as a garnish with other foods or used to flavor dishes. This is a chinese equivalence to strong cheese.
originalName: Fu yu, fǔ rǔ, 腐乳

name: gai lán
aliases: gai lán, jiè lán, 芥兰
description: Chinese Broccoli; usually steamed and served with oyster sauce
originalName: gai lán, jiè lán, 芥兰

name: General Tso Chicken
summary: a western dish of chicken covered in sweet sauce
description: A dish of corn starch battered deep fried chicken covered in sweet sauce. This dish is not chinese in origin, but rather a creation of overseas chinese restaurants to cater for western palates. General Tso may refer to a Qing dynasty statesman, but there is no substantiated ties to the chicken dish.

name: ghon chow ow ho
aliases: ghon chow ow ho, gān chǎo niú hé, 乾炒牛河
summary: Stir fried flat rice noodles with beef and vegetables
description: Stir fried flat rice noodles with beef and vegetables. A typically Cantonese dish.
originalName: ghon chow ow ho, gān chǎo niú hé, 乾炒牛河

name: Gohn Yiu Cheu
aliases: Gohn Yiu Cheu, qián yáo zhù, 乾瑤柱
description: Preserved dried scallop, oftentimes reconstituted, and used to flavor various dishes.
originalName: Gohn Yiu Cheu, qián yáo zhù, 乾瑤柱

name: Gou Ji
description: Steamed dumplings; can include various ingredients but is usually made with ground pork. Wrapping is a simple flour wrapping and the dumplings are steamed and can be dipped in chili oil, soy sauce, and vinegar.

name: Gung Pao Gai ding
aliases: Gung Pao Gai ding, gōng bǎo jī, 宫保鸡丁
description: Spicy Chicken dish, stir fried with chilies, peppercorns, vegetables, and either cashews or peanuts. This is a Szechuan dish.
originalName: Gung Pao Gai ding, gōng bǎo jī, 宫保鸡丁

name: Ha Gow
aliases: Ha Gow, há jiǎo, 蝦餃
description: A dim sum of steamed shrimp dumplings wrapped in a translucent rice skin
originalName: Ha Gow, há jiǎo, 蝦餃

name: Haam Daan
aliases: Haam Daan, xián dàn, 鹹蛋
description: Salted Duck Eggs are preserved by brining process and used often in various dishes. The whites are very salty, but the yolks are less so.
originalName: Haam Daan, xián dàn, 鹹蛋

name: Haam Sui Gaau
aliases: Haam Sui Gaau, xián shuǐ jiǎo, 鹹水餃
description: A steamed dumpling filled with meat, chopped vegetables, and peanut in a rice flour skin
originalName: Haam Sui Gaau, xián shuǐ jiǎo, 鹹水餃

name: Haam yu
aliases: Haam yu, xián yú, 鹹魚
description: Hard, Salt Cured dried fish often used to flavor dishes or simply steamed and eaten with rice.
originalName: Haam yu, xián yú, 鹹魚

name: haau yu gap
aliases: haau yu gap, kǎo rǔ gē, 烤乳鴿
originalName: haau yu gap, kǎo rǔ gē, 烤乳鴿

name: Ho yow siu bak choy
aliases: Ho yow siu bak choy, háo yóu xiǎo bái cài, 蠔油小白菜
summary: young Bok Choy in oyster sauce
originalName: Ho yow siu bak choy, háo yóu xiǎo bái cài, 蠔油小白菜

name: Ho yow
aliases: Ho yow, háo yóu, 蠔油
description: Oyster Sauce; often used as a cooking seasoning as well as a condiment for vegetables.
originalName: Ho yow, háo yóu, 蠔油

name: Hoi jeet
aliases: Hoi jeet, hǎi zhē, 海蜇
description: Jellyfish is a dim sum dish; it's dried, salted, reconstituted and blanched in a series of steps, then seasoned lightly with vinegar and sesame oil. It is often served cold. It has a unique chewy and crunchy texture; similar to cooked cartilage from chicken.
originalName: Hoi jeet, hǎi zhē, 海蜇

name: hoi saam
aliases: hoi saam, hǎi cān, 海參
description: Sea Cucumber is a bottom dwelling invertebrate that is braised slowly until the meat is soft and almost melts. It's served typically in a rich thick sauce, sometimes with mushrooms or other vegetables.
originalName: hoi saam, hǎi cān, 海參

name: Hoi Seen jeark chou
aliases: Hoi Seen jeark chou, hǎi xiān què cháo, 海鲜雀巢
description: Not to be mistaken for Yeen Woa (燕窩), Seafood birds nest is simply a dish of stir fried seafood (fish, calamari, shrimp, and/or scallop) in a simple sauce, served in a "nest" of deep fried shoe string taro.
originalName: Hoi Seen jeark chou, hǎi xiān què cháo, 海鲜雀巢

name: Hoisin jeung
aliases: Hoisin jeung, hǎi xiān jiàng, 海鮮醬
description: "seafood sauce" made of sweet potato
originalName: Hoisin jeung, hǎi xiān jiàng, 海鮮醬

name: Hung dou sah
aliases: Hung dou sah, gōng dòu shā, 紅豆沙
summary: A dessert of sweet red bean soup
description: Red beans cooked into a soup, sweetened and possibly mixed with various grains, lotus flower, and/or citrus peel for flavor.
originalName: Hung dou sah, gōng dòu shā, 紅豆沙

name: Hung Dou Sah
aliases: Hung Dou Sah, gōng dòu shā, 紅豆沙
description: A very common Cantonese dessert. Sometimes served with sago (西米)
originalName: Hung Dou Sah, gōng dòu shā, 紅豆沙

name: Hung Sui
aliases: Hung Sui, gōng shāo, 紅烧
description: Referring to dishes that are slow cooked in sweetened soy sauce.
originalName: Hung Sui, gōng shāo, 紅烧

name: Hut Tow Ha
aliases: Hut Tow Ha, hé táo xiā, 核桃虾
description: A western and Hong Kong Chinese dish, this usually involves deep frying shrimp in a cornstarch and egg batter, sweet glazed walnuts, and mixing in a mayonnaise based sauce.
originalName: Hut Tow Ha, hé táo xiā, 核桃虾

name: Ja Jeung Mein
aliases: Ja Jeung Mein, Zhajiang mian, 炸醬面
summary: Spicy noodles with minced meat sauce
description: A spicy noodle dish served at wonton restaurants. It's typically noodles with a spicy meat sauce; more tangy than dan dan mein; its szechuan counterpart.
originalName: Ja Jeung Mein, Zhajiang mian, 炸醬面

name: Jeaung cha aap
aliases: Jeaung cha aap, Zhang cha yā, 樟茶鴨
description: A traditional Szechuan dish of duck marinated with spices (peppercorns, ginger, garlic, salt) and then cooked and smoked in black tea.
originalName: Jeaung cha aap, Zhang cha yā, 樟茶鴨

name: Ji Ma Wu
aliases: Ji Ma Wu, zhī má hú, 芝麻糊
description: A chinese dessert soup made of blended sesame seads with sugar added. Tong Yuan (sweet rice balls) are often added
originalName: Ji Ma Wu, zhī má hú, 芝麻糊

name: jiang choi
aliases: jiang choi, jiang cai, 醬菜
description: Pickled vegetables, often used as a garnish for flavoring more bland foods like soy soup or congee.
originalName: jiang choi, jiang cai, 醬菜

name: Jing gai yuk bo jai faan
aliases: zhēng jī ròu bào zǐ fàn
Jing gai yuk bo jai faan, zhēng jī ròu bào zǐ fàn, 蒸雞肉煲仔飯
originalName: Jing gai yuk bo jai faan, zhēng jī ròu bào zǐ fàn, 蒸雞肉煲仔飯

name: jing yú
aliases: jing yú, zhēng yú, 蒸魚
description: Steamed fish is a fundamental dish of chinese home cooking. Whole fish (many varieties) are simply steamed with sliced scallions and ginger and hot oil and soy sauce are poured over the top.
originalName: jing yú, zhēng yú, 蒸魚

name: jiu yeem gwat
aliases: jiu yeem gwat, jiāo yán gǔ, 椒鹽骨
originalName: jiu yeem gwat, jiāo yán gǔ, 椒鹽骨

name: jiu yeem haa
aliases: jiu yeem haa, jiāo yán há, 椒鹽蝦
originalName: jiu yeem haa, jiāo yán há, 椒鹽蝦

name: jiu yeem yow yu
aliases: jiu yeem yow yu, jiāo yán yóu yú, 椒鹽魷魚
originalName: jiu yeem yow yu, jiāo yán yóu yú, 椒鹽魷魚

name: Juk
description: 粥 "Jook" can be eaten any time of the day and is served often as a fast food. Traditionally, it is a useful way to finish off the scrapings of a rice pot and leftover rice by adding simple ingredients for flavoring. Common ingredients include seafood, raw egg, sliced beef, shredded pork, and thousand year eggs.

name: Jung Zi
summary: Glutinous Rice wrapped in banana leaf
description: Glutinous Rice wrapped in banana leaf. This dish is similar to the dim sum variety of Lotus Leaf Rice (Lo Mai Gai 糯米雞), but more dense and larger.

name: Laap aap
aliases: Laap aap, là yā, 臘鴨
description: Duck meat that is dried and salt cured then reconstituted by steaming or other method to be eaten alone or as a flavoring for other dishes.
originalName: Laap aap, là yā, 臘鴨

name: laap cheung
aliases: laap cheung, là cháng, 蠟肠
description: Chinese sausage, sweet cured dry sausage, used in many dishes after being softened by steaming.
originalName: laap cheung, là cháng, 蠟肠

name: laap mei bao jai faan
aliases: laap mei bao jai faan, là wèi bào zǐ fàn, 蠟味煲仔飯
summary: Clay Pot with Chinese Sausage over rice
description: Clay Pot with Chinese Sausage over rice; may be general preserved meats as well; duck, liver sausage, and cured chinese bacon. Clay Pot dishes are common street or comfort food in Hong Kong.
originalName: laap mei bao jai faan, là wèi bào zǐ fàn, 蠟味煲仔飯

name: laap mei bou jai
aliases: laap mei bou jai, là mùi bào zǐ fàn, 蠟味煲仔飯
description: Served in a scalding hot clay pot, this dish is preserved meats (sausage, pork belly, preserved duck) slow cooked in sauce and baked over rice.
originalName: laap mei bou jai, là mùi bào zǐ fàn, 蠟味煲仔飯

name: Laap yuk
aliases: Laap yuk, là ròu, 臘肉
description: Pork meat that is dried and salt cured then reconstituted by steaming or other method to be eaten alone or as a flavoring for other dishes.
originalName: Laap yuk, là ròu, 臘肉

name: Lai Lui Ha
aliases: Lai Lui Ha, lā niào há, 拉尿蝦
description: "Pissing shrimp" is the cantonese nickname for Mantis shrimp, a mean looking crustacean which resembles a cross between a very large shrimp and a lobster, but with an extremely spiny shell. The Mantis shrimp is also incredibly fast in its reflexes; its claws strike faster than any animal motion on earth and have been known to shatter aquirium glass. Steamed or deep fried, mantis shrimp produce delicious meat similar to lobster.
originalName: Lai Lui Ha, lā niào há, 拉尿蝦

name: ling yue kow
aliases: ling yue kow, líng yú cầu, 鯪魚球
description: Made of fish puree, dace fish balls are deep fried and served on bamboo skewers
originalName: ling yue kow, líng yú cầu, 鯪魚球

name: lo bak goh
aliases: lo bak goh, luó bó gāo, 蘿蔔糕
description: A savory dim sum of turnip turned into a mash like cake, mixed with dried shrimps, chopped scallion, and diced barbeque pork, then pan fried until crip on the outside.
originalName: lo bak goh, luó bó gāo, 蘿蔔糕

name: lo foh tong
aliases: lo foh tong, lǎo huǒ shāng, 老火湯
description: Literally "old fire soup", this soup is a slow cooked broth made with various vegetables and pork or bones. Root vegetables like lotus root is often an ingredient.
originalName: lo foh tong, lǎo huǒ shāng, 老火湯

name: Lo mein
aliases: Lo mein, lāo mian, 撈麵
summary: "Mixed Noodles" - a noodle dish of Hong Kong
description: A dish of blanched egg noodles served with various toppings of meat and vegetables. A side of broth is provided and the diner can choose the amount of dryness preferred, along with common preferred additions of ginger, oyster sauce, or vinegar. The term "Lo-Mein" in parts of the US (midwest and east) is interchangeably used with Chow mein; pan fried noodles, but is not the correct usage by cantonese cooking.
originalName: Lo mein, lāo mian, 撈麵

name: Lo Po Beng
aliases: Lo Po Beng, lǎo pó bǐng, 老婆饼
description: A classic Cantonese pastry which is made of flaky dough filled with wintermelon and almond paste. The origin of the name comes from the story of a poor man who's wife sold herself to slavery to buy him medicine. When the man recovered, he created these cakes to sell, earning enough to buy his wife back.
originalName: Lo Po Beng, lǎo pó bǐng, 老婆饼

name: lou mai gai
aliases: lou mai gai, nuò mǐ jī, 糯米雞
summary: Glutanous Rice wrapped in a lotus leaf; a Dim Sum
description: A dim sum dish of glutanous rice wrapped around minced meat and sometimes a salted duck egg yolk. The handful sized ball is wrapped in a lotus leaf and steamed soft and moist.
originalName: lou mai gai, nuò mǐ jī, 糯米雞

name: Low han zhai
aliases: Low han zhai, Low han zhai, 罗汉斋

facts: Ma stands for "mazi" (Pinyin: mázi Traditional Chinese 麻子,) which means a person disfigured by pockmarks. Po (Chinese 婆) translates as "old woman". Hence, Ma Po is an old woman whose face was pockmarked. Legend says that the pock-marked old woman (má pó) was a widow who lived in the Chinese city of Chengdu. Due to her condition, her home was placed on the outskirts of the city. By coincidence, it was near a road where traders often passed. Although the rich merchants could afford to stay within the numerous inns of the prosperous city while waiting for their goods to sell, poor farmers would stay in cheaper inns scattered along the sides of roads on the outskirts of the ancient city.

description: Originating from southern france, cassoulet is a slow cooked bean stew cooked with sausage or bacon, making a hearty dish.

name: charcuterie
summary: pork products such as sausage, ham, and patê

name: charcutière (sauce)
summary: A sauce of onion sautéed in butter and blended into demi-glace consummé and white wine
description: A sauce of onion sautéed in butter and blended into demi-glace consummé and white wine

name: château
summary: a steak cut from sirloin or rib

name: châteaubriand
summary: very large thick steak, grilled to serve two, served with flavored butter
description: very large thick steak, grilled to serve two, served with flavored butter

name: chausson aux pommes
summary: An apple pastry with flaky dough shell

name: chicorée
description: a category of vegetable which includes endives, radicchio, and escarole. Chicory root from some species is used as a substitute for coffee.

name: chocolat
description: chocolate: cultivated by Aztecs as a bitter drink called xocolātl, chocolate was brought to Europe originally by Spanish conquistadors. Xocolātl was often flavored with vanilla and was considered a prized drink and continued to be consumed as a drink primarily into the 1700s. Dutch chocolatiers then created processes to extract cocoa butter to produce the confection we know today as chocolate.

name: choucroute
description: sauerkraut - soured cabbage, sometimes spiced with garlic and other herbs; generally considered a german food

name: cochon de lait
summary: young pig with more tender meat.

name: confit
summary: General term of foods preserved in a fluid, like fats
description: Confits refer to foods that are preserved by immersion in a substance like fats or liquids for preservation. Typically, the common associations are with goose confit d'oie) and duck (confit de canard). The meat is preserved in its own fat and then cooked in this to a very soft consistency.

name: Consommé
description: A clarified broth, often used as a base for other soups or dishes. Consommé differs from straight broth in that is is clarified by a process of adding egg white to a broth. The egg white creates foamy scum, binding with the egg white (albumin) all the small particles of vegetable or meat used to flavor the broth. The clear consommé below is poured out.

name: Coq au vin
summary: Chicken dish cooked with wine mushroom and onion

name: coquilles Saint-Jacques
description: scallops, literally translated as Scallops of Saint James. The scallop shell was the symbol for the crusader knights, their patron saint was James, brother of apostle John. Legend has it that he saved a drowning knight, who emerged from the sea covered in scallop shells.

name: coulis
description: purée; of a fruit or vegetable that can be savory or sweet; can be used as sauce for entrees or desserts.

name: Crème brûlée
summary: Custard dessert with a top of burnt sugar
description: Custard dessert with a top of burnt sugar. Literally means "burnt cream"

name: Crème fraîche
description: Crème fraîche literally translated is "fresh cream", but is actually soured with bacterial culture. It is thicker and milder than the american version and is often used in soups or in desserts

name: Crépe
summary: thin pancakes made with a variety of ingredients, sweet or savory

name: Crépe Suzette
description: A classic dessert crêpe with a warm sauce made with caramelized sugar, orange peel, juice, and liqueur (usually Grand Marnier) and flambéed (alchohols are lit on fire).

name: crêperie
summary: a place that specializes in crêpes

name: crevettes (grises, roses)
description: shrimps, prawns. The distinction between shrimp and prawn is not clearly defined in food circles. generally speaking one may consider prawns to raised in brackish (part fresh, part salt) water

name: croissant
description: flaky doughed pastry commonly served for breakfast. May be spread with fruit spreads or butter. Story has it that the croissant appeared in france after the battle of Tours in 732 with muslim forces, and its moon shape resembles the Islamic crescent.E308

name: croque au sel, á la
summary: foods eaten plainly with sea salt, raw

name: Croque Madam
summary: grilled ham and cheese sandwich with egg

name: croquembouche
summary: crunchy pastry filled with cream and topped with caramel
description: A dessert of profiteroles (choux pastry filled with pastry cream) presented as a tower and topped with decorative edible toppings including caramel, powdered sugar, chocolate, or nuts.

name: Croquette
summary: A cake of potato mixed with meats, vegetables, cheese, egg, and coated with breadcrumb
description: A cake of potato mixed with meats, vegetables, cheese, egg, and coated with breadcrumb

name: croûte
summary: toasted bread pieces accompanying different dishes or toppings
description: toasted bread pieces accompanying different dishes or toppings

name: crudités
summary: raw vegetables, often served with dip

name: cuire bleu
summary: a dish or rare cooked steak

name: cuisson
summary: cooking, or liquid used in cooking

name: cuvée
summary: a vat, as in the large cooking vessel, or the contents

name: cyrano
summary: consommé of duck with pieces of pressed duck meat covered with sauce and cheese
description: consommé of duck with pieces of pressed duck meat covered with sauce and cheese

name: daube
summary: A classic french stew of beef
description: A classic french stew of beef with mediterranean origins. It is often cooked with seasonings of provencal style like olives and lavender. Typically red wine vegetables and garlic are part of the seasoning. In some parts of france, cuts of bulls killed in bull fights are typically used for daube.

name: dauphinois, á la
summary: sliced potato baked with cream and cheese

name: daurade
description: sea bream is a small fish with delicate white flaky meat and skin. It's often sold as dorado or dorade and is a saltwater fish.

name: déglacer
description: to deglaze, the cooking act of reducing the deeply cooked drippings off a pan surface by pouring cold fluid, wine or broth, onto a hot pan after browning meat

name: Délice de Bourgogne
summary: A creamy cheese with rind similar to Brie

name: delice des dieu
summary: "Delight of the Gods" a fruit and lady finger cake

name: demi-glace
summary: a brown sauce made by reducing meats
description: a brown sauce made by reducing meats; demi-glace is used as a flavor base for making sauces

name: derby
summary: stuffed chicken dish enriched with truffle, foie gras, broth, sweet wine, and veal stock
description: stuffed chicken dish enriched with truffle, foie gras, broth, sweet wine, and veal stock

name: Digestif
summary: drink served after meals to help digestion
description: drink served after meals to help digestion - may contain herbs believed to aid digestion

name: duxelles
summary: A blend of mushroom shallot and herbs made into a paste
description: A blend of mushroom shallot, butter, and herbs made into a paste and used in stuffed dishes or roulades.

name: eau
description: bottle of water: une bouteille de eau, hot water: eau chaude, mineral water: eau minérale, sparkling water: eau gazeuse, still water: eau non-gazeuse

name: éclair
summary: A pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate
description: A cylindrical pastry made with choux dough for its airy consistency, and filled with a sweet cream and topped with chocolate. Often the filling is made with a custard or coffee flavored cream as well.

name: écrevisses
description: crayfish, crawfish: small crustacean related to lobster. Found in fresh water as bottom dwellers. Meat is similar in texture to lobster. Species can be found all over the world in brackish or freshwater.

name: endive
summary: Endive is a kind of vegetable with crispy leaves that can be used in salads or cooked. It is also known as chicory.
description: Endive is a kind of vegetable with crispy leaves that can be used in salads or cooked. It is also known as chicory.

name: escalope
summary: A cutlet of meat, Scallop Shell in old French
description: Escalope refers to a cutlet or fillet of meat. Typically this is Veal, but may include other "white" meats like fish and game. They may be stuffed like Cordon Bleu. Italian form of escalope would include Scallopine.

name: escarole
summary: A type of endive with lacy, frilly leaves

name: Escoffier, Georges Auguste
description: Georges Auguste Escoffier (1846 - 1935) popularized and updated traditional french cooking methods. He was a chef and restaurantier credited with the organization system of brigade de cuisine, the basis of French kitchen structure. His associations with César Ritz popularized french haute cuisine in Paris and London.

name: Espagnole
summary: A dark brown sauce made with veal reduction and roux
description: A classic sauce made of veal reduction and roux. Often tomato is added. Espagnole is considered on of the 4 classic french sauces along with Veloute, Allemande, and Béchamel.

name: Étouffée
summary: A Cajun dish of seafood in sauce over rice
description: Meaning "smothered" in French, Étouffée is a Cajun dish (American state of Louisiana) of shellfish cooked in rich mild pepper based sauce covering rice.

name: filet mignon
summary: a small cut of beef from the tip of the tenderloin
description: a small cut of beef from the tip of the tenderloin. The tenderloins are two strips of muscle running along the length of the back. Filet Mignon is a lower fat cut with some of the best tenderness.

name: Filet Mignon
summary: Cut of meat which is the tenderloin
description: commonly served as steak

name: financier
summary: a small tea cake made of butter flower and almond
description: A light cake made in shaped molds served as a tea cake, financiers are made of almond paste and beurre noissette. The name originates possibly from some original square shapes similar to gold bars, or from the origins of bakeries in Paris' financial district.

name: flambé
description: flavoring a dish with alchohol and using flame to ignite it, leaving the essence (flavor) of the spirits in the food

name: Flamiche
description: a quiche with leeks - quiche is a egg based tart, often made with vegetables, cheese or meat.

name: fleur de sel
summary: "flower of salt"-hand collected sea salt from Brittany

name: foie (gras)
description: liver, Foie gras is fattened liver of goose. It may be served sliced and grilled as a topping or accompaniment with other meats, or as patê, the more common caked version

name: fondant
summary: In pastry, a sugar confection used in cake decoration
description: In pastry making fondant is a sugar and cream paste, colored, and used to decorate cakes.

name: francese
summary: A dish of meat, battered and fried, with lemon sauce

name: Fricassée
summary: stew of meat and vegetables in a cream sauce

name: garbure
summary: A hearty soup of vegetables and bacon

name: Gâteau
description: Cake; of the traditional sense of sponge cake in layers over cream or fruits

name: gratin, au grautin
summary: A term referring to style of baking foods in cream sauce with breadcrumb topping
description: A term referring to style of baking foods in cream sauce with breadcrumb topping. Gratin refers to a crust, whether that is of cheese or breadcrumb.

name: Gruyère
summary: Hard Swiss cheese of cows milk
description: Gruyère can be served in various stages of ripeness, with more flavor imparted with greater age. It can be used as a good melting cheese, adding strong flavor and aroma.

name: hors d' oeuvre
summary: small dishes served cold at the start of meals or to accompanying drinks

name: langoustines
summary: scampi Italian) - a type of crustacean resembling a small lobster
description: a crustacean similar to small lobster, al scampi means a dish is made with lobster or with the scampi. Also known in France as langoustine. They are saltwater crustaceans caught in the atlantic. Distinct by the presence of fore-claws.

name: Le Cordon Bleu
summary: A premier French hospitality school, "blue ribbon"
description: Literally "blue ribbon", the Cordon Bleu is the premier french school of cooking. The modern school dates back to the late 1800's, but the origins of the term goes back to the middle ages. The school has many notable graduates in the culinary world. A dish named Chicken Cordon Bleu is not related to the school, but that is a roulade of chicken breast, breaded and pounded flat, rolled with ham and swiss cheese, and baked.

name: mache
description: A type of soft lettuce that is more sweet in taste with very delicate leaves.

name: Meuniére
summary: battered, deep fried, and served with sauce of lemon butter and parsley

name: Mille-feuille
summary: Meaning Thousand Leaf; thin layered pastry dough
description: Meaning Thousand Leaf; thin layered puff pastry dough. Traditionally prepared there would be 729 layers.

name: mirepoix
summary: a blend of fine chopped vegetables and ham or bacon
description: a blend of fine chopped vegetables and ham or bacon, used as a platform for braising meats

name: Mornay
description: A creamy cheese sauce. "Béchemel" is a cream sauce and the Mornay is further flavored by cheese such as Gruyére

name: Moules Marinières
summary: mussels cooked with shallots in white wine sauce

name: mousse
summary: A whipped mixture of egg and cream and flavoring
description: Typically a dessert of whipped cream egg and flavoring, though classic mousse consists only of egg yolks, egg whites, sugar, and chocolate or other flavorings, without the cream. Modern variations may have mousse made savory with meats such as fish.

name: noir
summary: black (color, as well as for coffee)

name: oignen
description: Onion, one of the world's most commonly consumed and oldest cultivated vegetables, has many varieties and many uses. Many onions are high in sugar content which is why they caramalize when cooked. Shallots are a form of onion and a mainstay of western and southeast asian cooking. Green onions, also known as scallions, are chopped onion shoots.

name: olives
description: olive; the olive is a fruit of the olive tree, native to the mediterranean region. It is rich in oils that are used throughout cooking. When harvested, they are typically green and have a bitter taste. Processes of fermentation or curing are used to remove bitterness and add taste. Common fermenation involves soaking in vinegar, salt, and water, or curing in salt, lye, or fresh water dissolution of the bitter phenolic compounds.

name: pâté
description: can refer to the pressed liver cake or a general term for pie

name: Pâte à choux
summary: Choux pastry, an airy pastry dough of butter, water, flour, and eggs
description: Choux pastry, an airy pastry dough of butter, water, flour, and eggs. Used to make a variety of pastries including croquembouche, profiteroles, and eclairs.

name: Pâtes
description: pasta - not to be mistaken for paté (without "s")

name: Pérgourdine, à la
summary: style of beef or chicken with truffles

name: pistou
summary: pesto: the italian sauce of basil olive oil pinenuts and garlic
description: pesto: the italian sauce of basil olive oil pinenuts and garlic

name: Poivre, au
summary: Made with a Pepper sauce (poivre: pepper)

name: pommes château
summary: potato pieces simply boiled and flavored with salt and butter; an accompaniment to steak
description: potato pieces simply boiled and flavored with salt and butter; an accompaniment to steak

name: pommes Dauphine
description: Potato puffs made by mashing potatoes and blending with choux pastry dough (same dough used in cream puffs and profiteroles), then deep frying.

name: pommes fondant
summary: A baked dish of mash potato with an au gratin topping
description: A dish of mashed potato that is creamed and seasoned then baked with breadcrumb

name: pommes tournées
summary: Potatoes, skinned and roasted or steamed, served in a long oval shape
description: Potatoes, skinned and roasted or steamed, served in a long oval shape

name: praline
summary: A confection of nuts and carmelized sugar

name: quiche
summary: A baked egg tart in flaky crust
description: Baked tarts (like a pie) with egg and cream based filling and ingredients can include meats (bacon) and cheese, or vegetables in other forms. Quiche Lorraine is the classic with the egg and cream mixed with chopped bacon. Add onion for Quiche Alsacienne.

name: Ragoût
summary: A stew of meat and vegetables
description: Derived from the word ragoûter which means to revive, ragoût refers to stews which are main dishes and may be made with or without meat, using slow cooking to enhance flavors

name: Ratatouille
description: A vegetable stew of eggplant, tomato, zucchini, and garlic.

name: relais routier
summary: truck stop café, often selling hot foods

name: rémoulade
description: A condiment that often accompanies fish, rémoulade is a mayonnaise based sauce that can be flavored with different ingredients but chiefly will include garlic, capers, and anchovies.

name: rillettes
summary: a soft meat spread for bread
description: Rillettes are soft meat spreads meant to accompany bread; related to pâté. It is made by cooking meats in fat, slowly until the meat is spreadable soft. Excess fat is drained away, leaving a soft congealed cake that may be seasoned then chilled into a paste. Various meats can be used including pork or poultry (duck).

name: rouille
summary: "rust" sauce, a spread for bread, typically accompanying bouillabaisse
description: A spread for bread made from olive oil, breadcrumbs, garlic, saffron, and chilies. This is a spread which commonly accompanies bread and served with bouillabase.

name: roulade
summary: A broad term for rolled dishes, savory or sweet
description: A roll, as in cake or pastry with cream or pasta with meat, or flattened meat cutlet with filling. It is usually baked, then served sliced so that the spirals of the roll and filling are seen.

name: roux
summary: a blend of butter of flour, base of sauces
description: a common base of sauce, roux is a thickening agent for sauces.

name: roux
summary: A sauce or base of wheat flour and clarified butter

name: sabayon
summary: Dessert of liquor and eggyolk sauce over fresh fruit
description: French word for zabaglione

name: saint pierre
summary: A kind of fish also called a John Dory

name: salon de thé
summary: tea shop; serves pastries, salads, and other small eats

name: sauce choron
summary: béarnaise sauce made with tomato purée

name: sauce pérgourdine
summary: sauce périgueux made with foie gras
description: sauce périgueux (demi-glace, truffle, and Madiera Wine, but made with foie gras.

name: sauce périgueux
description: sauce made from demi-glace, truffle and Madiera wine

name: saucisson sec
description: Dried Sausage, generally pork. Simply seasoned with pepper and garlic, this is the french version of Italian salumi.

name: saumon
description: salmon: pink fleshed fish that spawns in freshwater rivers, then migrates and matures in open ocean. The return to spawn in the same waters of their birth before dying. Salmon is best consumed wild caught for better flavor. However due to scarcity, much salmon served is farmed and its pink color is derived from feed. Salmon is found in several oceans and has many varieties. Farmed salmon should be carefully considered; much of the farming yields fish with high levels of toxins, parasites, and pesticides. Improper salmon farming may also create heavy environmental impact that threatens wild salmon populations.

name: saur
description: smoked herring. Also called sardines in the US, herring are small silvery fish with high fat content meat. They are found in large schools with various species in the atlantic, pacific, and baltic seas.

name: savoie
summary: a spongy cake from the Savoy region

name: Soufflé
summary: A delicate baked dish made with egg; may be sweet or savory
description: A delicate baked dish made with egg that may be sweet or savory. Egg whites are whipped full of air and rise in the oven. Soufflé may be flavored with cheeses, chocolate, or fruit jams.

name: tapenade
summary: A southern french puree of olive caper and anchovie
description: Tapenade is mainly olive, puree ground with caper anchovie and oil to be used as a bread topping.

name: tapénade
summary: a purée of olives, capers, anchovies, and olive oil

name: Tartare (Steak)
summary: dish of raw minced meat (beef usually) egg yolk, and onion
description: dish of raw minced meat (beef usually) egg yolk, and onion. May also be made with raw tuna (thon)

name: tarte Flambee
summary: a "pie" of bread dough baked with crème fraiche, bacon, and onion.
description: a "pie" of bread dough baked with crème fraiche, bacon, and onion. Originates from the Alsace region (near germany) and is Flammkuchen in German. So named because it should be baked in a high temperature open flame oven.

name: tartine
summary: A bite sized snack of crisped bread, topped with various ingredients, a form of hors d' oeuvre
description: A topped piece of bread or with ingredients that may be savory or sweet. May include jams, honey, or flavored ingredients like pâté, chopped truffled olives, or caviar. Meant to stimulate drinking.

name: Terrine
description: a category of dishes of compressed meats, cooked in earthenware containers called "terrine", sometimes served at room temperature. Paté is a common form of Terrine

name: tomate
description: A fruit native to South America with many many varieties

name: torchon
summary: "towel"-refers to a method of cooking foie gras
description: "towel" in french, refers to a method of cooking foie gras in a towel

name: tourte, torte
summary: A pie or a cake, may be sweet or savory

name: truffes
description: truffles - rare mushrooms, extremely strong flavored, traditionally found growing in dark damp forested wilderness, sometimes under dirt. Special pigs are trained to sniff them out. Often times truffle infused oils are used for cooking and flavoring

name: Velouté
summary: A classic velvety sauce made of roux (butter and flour) and broth
description: A classic velvety sauce made of roux (butter and flour) and light broth. Veloute is considered on of the 4 classic french sauces along with Allemande, Béchamel, and Espagnole.

name: verre
summary: glass (as in a glass of wine)
description: glass (as in a glass of red \wine): un verre de vin rouge

name: Vichyssoise
summary: A soup of leeks, cream, potato, onion, and stock

name: vin - blancs, rouges, de dessert, mousseux
description: wine, Vin blanc: white wine, Vin rouge: red wine, Vin de dessert: dessert wine, Vin mousseux: sparking wine
originalName: vin - blancs, rouges, de dessert, mousseux

name: vin de pays
summary: "country wine" - Label assigned to higher quality wines.
description: Label assigned to higher quality wines helping to specify origin and composition of grape. Vin de pays designated wines are tested more thoroughly and must conform to standards in comparison to Vin de Table wines. There are many standards for Vin de Pays which include percentage of grape variety as well as geographic origin, alchohol levels, quantity of sulfur dioxide, and yield of crop per hectare of land. Governed by the AOC.

name: vin de table
description: table wine - designation of wine that does not necessarily have specifc grape composition

name: Aviyal
description: A Kerala dish of seasoned vegetables cooked in curry and coconut oil or milk along with a tart agent such as milk curd or tamarind. Common vegetables include yam, plantain or carrots.

name: badami
description: Almonds are the seeds (not actually a nut) of a fruit tree that has cultivation history dating back to the bronze age. It originates in the middle east and is now grown around the world in moderate climates. It is low in carbohydrate and high in monounsaturated fats and can be used as a good flour substitute in gluten free recipes. Almonds are used extensively in sweet and savory applications.

name: baingan bhartha
description: A dish of eggplant (brinjal) roasted soft, then mashed and blended with a variety of seasonings.

name: baingan, brinjal
description: Eggplant: a common produce which is actually a berry of a plant that has varieties grown in asia, europe, and the americas. It is related to the tobacco plant and contains small amounts of nicotine. Eggplant is also called aubergine commonly in europe.

name: bhatura
description: Deep Fried bread. May be made of wheat or white flour.

name: Bhel Puri
description: A Chaat dish of Puffed rice pillows topped with tomatoes onion, potato, and a tamarind sauce.

name: Biryani
description: An Indian dish with Middle Eastern origins, Biryani is a very broad term describing rice dishes that are seasoned with herbs and spices and cooked often with meats or vegetables.

name: Chaat
description: Small dishes meant to be fast food and served typically at specialized chaat restaurants

name: Chai
description: Means "spiced". An essential drink of India, served after meals or on the street by chaiwallahs (street vendors), Masala chai is spiced black tea and milk spiced and sweetened. Spices that may include: cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, pepper, ginger, allspice, coriander, caraway seeds, nutmeg.

name: Chana Masala (or Chola)
description: Spiced Chickpea stew; a staple dish

name: chapathi
description: A flat bread of unleavened wheat flour and water cooked in a pan. Depending on region this is also called a "roti"

name: Chola Bhatura
description: Fried bread (bhatura) served with spiced chickpea (Chana Masala).

name: Chutney, or Catni चटनी
description: Chutney is a category of condiments that are made from various ingredients that may be fruits or vegetables crushed and likely blended with sugars, vinegar, or other spices to flavor and or preserve.

name: dhaal
description: Lentils, often in a stew form, curried and possibly mixed with other vegetables such as spinach or mustard greens (saag dhaal), cream and spices (dhaal Makhani)

name: Dosa
description: The Dosa or Dosay is a South Indian thin crepe using flour of ground rice and black lentils. It is cooked with ghee (clarified butter) and eaten for breakfast or dinner. Various fillings can be used; often vegetables.

name: garam masala
description: "hot paste" of peppercorn, cumin, bay, star anise, nutmeg, coriander, and possibly other spices by regional variation.

name: ghee
description: Clarified butter used commonly in cooking

name: Idli
summary: Steamed rice and lentil cakes served with various sauces
description: Idli is a common south indian staple: steamed disc shaped buns made of a flour mixture of ground rice and black lentil. It is served with various chutney or sambar (Vegetable stew)

name: kofta
summary: Ball of meat or wheat/grain in sauce

name: Korma
description: Curry dish made creamy with yoghurt or coconut milk, milder flavor. Can be made with various meats or vegetables

name: Makhani
description: general category of dishes with creamy or buttery sauces prepared with spices or yogurt

name: masala मसाला
description: A generic term for mixed spices. Dishes such as chicken tikka masala, or drinks such as chai masala simply reference that they are spiced. Spices can start in powdered blends or pastes.

name: milagu rasam
description: Tomato based soup with tamarind, tumeric, pepper cumin, garlic, curry leaves, corriander, mustard and other ingredients

name: Murgh
description: chicken; a butter chicken dish would be "murgh makhani" or curry chicken would be "murgh korma"

name: Naan
description: Leavened (made with yeast) Flatbread baked in a tandoor.

name: Pakora
summary: A snack fried bite sized foods.
description: Battered bite sized snacks of deep fried chicken, paneer (farmers cheese), cauliflower, or other vegetables.

name: Paneer
description: Indian cheese is a "farmers cheese" produced by acid curdling milk with lemon juice or other food acids. If can come in many dishes and does not require rennet. It has similar texture to firm tofu.

name: Pani Puri
description: Puffed rice pillows topped with curried garbanzo (cholay) and or potatoes (aloo), topped with chutney and served with flavored water

name: Paratha
summary: A whole wheat flatbread, typically stuffed and pan fried.
description: Similar to a Roti, originating from southern indian food, Paratha is an unleavened wheat bread that is often stuffed with ingredients such as potato, cauliflower, or cheese, then fried.

name: Raita
description: Yoghurt based condiments that are flavored with herbs or spices such as cilantro, coriander, caraway seeds, cumin, or peppers. It is often used as a dip.

name: Roti
description: Unleavened (made without yeast) flatbread, made with various flours and may be cooked on flat grill surfaces or in earthenware stoves. Also called chapathi.

name: Saag
summary: a dish of spinach or mustard green stew
description: (Hindi: साग, Urdu: ساگ) Spinach or Mustard greens stew made with a variety of spices. Common additions to this stew include cheese (paneer), ghost (lamb), or murgh (chicken)

name: Sambar
summary: A vegetable dish cooked in tamarind and pigeon peas
description: A stew of various vegetables cooked with a broth base from tamarind and toovar dal (pigeon pea) and lentils. Various vegetables can be used (okra, pumpkin carrots, onion, potato, etc). It is accompanied by oils fried with dried chilis and other spices.

name: Samosa
description: Deep Fried dumpling usually stuffed with potato, peas, and spices, served with Tamarind chutney

name: Tandoor
description: Clay Oven, usually charcoal or wood fired, used to bake meats, vegetables, or leavened bread (naan). "Tandoori" often refers to foods cooked in a tandoor. An example would be the typical tandoori chicken (murgh) that is marinated (often bright red or yellow) and roasted in the tandoor.

name: Tikka
summary: chunk or cuts of meat, spiced and roasted
description: Tikka is often associated with chicken tikka masala,. A generic name for chicken chunks in any variety of spicy sauces. Or it may be referring to tandoor cooked meats that are spiced, often marinated to a red, orange, or yellow color.

name: Uttapam
description: An indian "pancake" made with a batter of rice and lentils and fermented. It is cooked with various ingredients with the batter.

name: Vada
summary: deep fried croquette of potato, lentil, or dhaal.
description: A south indian dish of deep fried cake of seasoned dhaal or potato, breaded with a light flour.

name: Carne Asada

name: Carne Guisada

name: Carnitas

name: cebolla
description: Onion, one of the world's most commonly consumed and oldest cultivated vegetables, has many varieties and many uses. Many onions are high in sugar content which is why they caramalize when cooked. Shallots are a form of onion and a mainstay of western and southeast asian cooking. Green onions, also known as scallions, are chopped onion shoots.

name: Ceviche
summary: An Appetizer of fish or shrimp marinated in lime until it is "cooked" without the application of heat

name: chapulines
description: spiced grasshoppers, toasted and seasoned and eaten as a popular snack

name: Chicharrón

name: Chilaquiles

description: A dish of tortillas, fried, then simmered in salsa. Chicken, egg, and/or cheese are added.

name: Chile Relleno
summary: A large chili pepper (usually Poblano) stuffed with cheese and fried
description: A dish of stuffed chili pepper, typically Poblano, filled with cheese or other meat. It is battered and deep fried.

name: Chile Verde
description: A stew of pork cooked in a green (verde) tomatillo sauce. Tomatillos are small green tomatoes cooked for sauces.

name: Chili Colorado
description: A beef stew in a brown sauce, marinated to a light spiciness in mild red chili paste

name: Chimichangas
description: A deep fried burrito, sometimes covered with melted cheese and sour cream

name: Chochinita Pibil
summary: a stew of slow roasted young pig
description: a stew of slow roasted young pork, marinated in citrus and cooked in a banana leaf.

name: Chorizo
description: Spicy mexican sausage that is soft and tender meat inside the casing. Often times beef and pork face meat and organs are used as filling for tenderness and richness.

name: Cóctel de camarón
description: Shrimp Cocktail: an appetizer consisting of a ring of blanch cooked, deveined and shelled shrimp ring the rim of a glass filled with a tomato salsa

name: Dulce de Leche
description: A caramel made by reducing sweetened milk under heat until a thick sweet sauce if left.

name: Empanadas
summary: A dumpling with pastry shell, fried. Can be sweet or savory.
description: A dumpling with pastry shell, fried. Empanadas of Mexico can be filled with sweets (mexican yam or pumpkin) or with savory ingredients (meats, cheese, beans, or vegetables).

name: Fajita
summary: a grill tossed blend of peppers, onion, and meat in chili spices
description: a grill tossed blend of peppers, onion, and meat in chili spices. Fajita is served with garnishes of guacamole, salsa (possibly pico de gallo), and avocado with tortillas.

name: Flan
summary: a rich egg custard dessert in a thin caramel sauce

name: frijoles refritos
description: Actually means well cooked beans. Made with mashed Pintos blended with lard, spice, and stock.

name: Gorditas
summary: Similar to a taco, but with a thick bread shell instead of a thin tortilla
description: meaning "little fat one", gorditas are effectively similar to a taco, but with a thicker round wrap grilled crispy.

name: Guacamole
summary: A mash of avocado and other garnishes
description: Mash of avocado, onion, cilantro, tomato, lime juice, and spices that may include chilis, pepper, and salt. Lime juice helps keep avocado from turning brown from oxidation.

name: Huevos Rancheros
description: A dish of eggs over corn tortillas, cooked with bell peppers and onion in tomato and chili salsa

name: Huitlacoche
description: fungus growing on corn, often used to make quesadillas

name: jalapeños
summary: spicy hot chili pepper, green or slightly red, commonly used for cooking
description: spicy hot chili pepper, green or slightly red, commonly used for cooking

name: jicama
summary: a root vegetable eaten raw in salads
description: Jicama is the root of a plant which grows as a vine. The texture is similar to apple or raw potato and has a light flavor as it consists mostly of water.

name: jitomate
summary: red tomato, also known as tomate rojo

name: Longaniza
summary: A sausage similar to chorizo, made of pork

name: machaca
summary: dish of very well cooked beef shredded in its own cooking juices
description: dish of very well cooked beef shredded in its own cooking juices. Machaca in its more traditional form is made with reconstituted dried meat. It is often served accompanying eggs.

name: Menudo
summary: A stew of tripe in a very rich spicy soup.
description: A stew of tripe in a rich soup that can be based on any number of ingredients including tomato, chili, and herbs including oregano and cilantro. Menudo is also the name of a popular early 80's Puerto Rican rock group which included a young Ricky Martin long before he was living La Vida Loca.

name: Migas
summary: A breakfast dish of eggs and tortillas
description: Migas (pronounced mi-yas) is a tex mex dish derived from Spanish and Portuguese origins. It means "crumbs" because leftover tortillas are torn up and cooked with eggs, chorizo, onions, chilis, and salsa, then served in tortillas. A meatless version is a traditional meal during Lent.

name: Milanesa
summary: Dishes of meat breaded and deep fried
description: Dishes of meat breaded and deep fried; may be pork cutlets or pounded beef.

name: Mole
summary: General term for "sauce", or commonly referring to a cocoa based sauce.
description: Mole is a general term for sauce, and there are many kinds. Mole in american terms is commonly associated with Mole Poblano, a thick sauce served over different meats, or simmered with different meats. Mole Poblano is prepared with a variety of dried chilies (Pasilla. Ancho, Chipotle, etc), along with ground nuts, cocoa (or mexican chocolate which is spiced with cinnamon), and other seasonings (avocado leaves, oregano, etc). The flavor is deeply nutty and earthy (not sweet as the chocolate may imply).

name: nachos
summary: A snack food of fried tortilla chips topped with spiced melted cheese
description: A snack food of fried tortilla chips topped with melted cheese, sliced jalepenos, and other toppings. Originally invented by mexican restaurant worker Ignacio Anaya.

name: nopales
description: a type of edible cactus, otherwise known as "prickly pear". Nopales is generally served cooked. It has a soft texture kind of like cooked bell pepper with a slippery feel like okra and is slightly tart. It's loaded with vitamins and fiber.

name: paste
summary: Small pastry filled with sweet or savory ingredients
description: Pastes are filled with anything from fruit such as pineapple or apple., to savory ingredients including beef, potatoes, or simply mole.

name: Pastel de Tres Leches
summary: a cake made with three kinds of milk and cream
description: Tres leches, or three creams, is a cake soaked in 3 kind of milk: evaporated, fresh, and condensed milks. The spongy cake is soaked in the milks and then cream is added to top it off.

name: Picadillo
summary: spiced ground beef; Typical Taco filling

name: Pico De Gallo
summary: A salsa of corse chopped vegetables
description: the "beak of the rooster" is a salsa consisting of tomatoes, onion, cilantro, lime juice, and possibly other additions to these essentials. It is usually corse chopped instead of blended.

name: Pozole
summary: A soup made with hominy, pork, and other ingredients
description: A soup often broth based, made with hominy, pork, onion, avocado, chili powder, and other ingredients

name: Quesadillas
summary: A dish of tortillas, sandwiching cheese and meat, and grilled
description: A dish of tortillas, sandwiching cheese and meat, and grilled. It can then be covered with sour cream, cheese, and guacamole.

name: queso oaxaca
summary: a mexican cheese, semi hard and mild in flavor
description: a mild white colored mexican cheese which has a texture similar to string cheese, similar to american mozzarella

name: res

name: Salsa Ranchera
description: ranch style sauce served warm and resembling a thick tomato based soup.

name: Salsa roja
summary: tomato based salsa cooked with many peppers to give the red color

name: Serrano
summary: A kind of chili, size of a small finger, in variety of colors

name: Sopes

description: A dish of corn meal cake (masas) grilled and topped with meat, sour cream, cheese, onion, and salsa

name: Tacos
summary: A dish of meat, cheese, cilantro, and salsa simply wrapped in a single fold corn tortilla
description: A dish of meat, cheese, cilantro, and salsa simply wrapped in one or two single fold corn tortilla. Sold in taqueria's or on streetside stands in mexico.

name: Tamales
summary: meat or cheese stuffed corn meal rolls
description: Tamales is a dish of corn meal rolls, stuffed with cheese or meat, then steamed in corn husks or other large plant leaves. It may be topped off with a ranchero style salsa and melted queso.

name: taquitos
summary: deep fried rolls of tortilla surrounding meats

name: tomate
summary: Tomato (green or verde), or jitomate for red tomato
description: Tomate generally refers to green tomatos, or specifically can be tomate verde. This herbacious plant originates from central and south america and exported to the rest of the world by the Spanish.

name: Tortas
description: A mexican sandwhich, made often with the same meats available to tacos, sandwiched in a split large white bread roll, or a crusty salted bread roll called bolillo. Typical fillings are similar to that of tacos such as sour cream, guacamole, lettuce, tomatoes, jalapenos, etc...

name: Tortilla
summary: Unleavened flat bread made simply on a grill
description: Unleavened flat bread made simply on a grill; may be flour or corn meal based and can be different sizes depending on the intended purpose of the tortilla

name: Tostadas
summary: A dish of deep fried tortillas covered with toppings
description: A dish of deep fried tortillas (corn) covered with various toppings like pico de gallo, sour cream, and avocado. Ceviche often is served as a tostada.

name: Totopos
description: fried pieces of tortilla, typically maiz, until crispy. Known in the US as tortilla chips.

name: tripas
description: Tripe refers to the cuts of sections of the intestinal track; often of beef. It can be sections of the stomach or intestines.

name: adobo
summary: a dry rub marinate for meats
description: A dry rub marinate for meats. Typical ingredients include chipotle pepper, tomato paste, lime, garlic, oregano, cumin, and vinegar. Related but different in flavor from adobo from the phillipines where meats are prepared with a vinegar base.

name: Apicius
summary: Title of Roman cookbooks from 4th and 5th century
description: Apicius is a series of books intended as a reference for culinary arts of Roman times in the mediterranean region. It is broken up into sections that cover various meats, the chef, and vegetables.

name: arctic char
summary: A cold water fish from canadian and alaskan waters
description: A coldwater fish from canadian and alaskan waters that is related to salmon and trout. It is both salt wand freshwater and yields meat that is red or pink.

name: arepa

name: Balut
summary: A Filipino delicacy of fertilized chicken egg
description: A common streetfood of southeast asia, balut is a fertilized raw egg which is eaten in various stages of development. It can be accompanied by hot sauce, vinegar, salt, sugar, lemon juice, or pepper.

name: bitters
summary: Alcoholic spirits that are bitter and often flavored
description: Bitters are typically used in mixed drinks and may be flavored to be sweetened or have essences of herbal or citrus.

name: bonito
summary: Class of fish belonging to Mackeral family
description: Class of fish belonging to mackerel family. In Japanese cooking outside japan, it is also known as skipjack tuna. Katsuo is the japanese pronounciation; served either raw, cooked, or as dried preserved shavings known as katsuobushi.

name: cape gooseberry
summary: A tart berry used in desserts, cultivated worldwide

name: chimichurri
description: South American based "green" sauce, made of minced herbs (oregano, parsley, cilantro, thyme), garlic, vinegar, and pepper. Can be used as a condiment or a marinate.

name: coriander
summary: General term for Cilantro, a soft fragrant herb

name: Curry
summary: An english word to describe spiced indian foods
description: Curry dishes are endless in variety but generally contain at least several of the spices Tumeric, cumin, coriander, fenugreek, and pepper.

name: fennel

name: Frappé

name: papusa
summary: Central American pancake of flour and cornmeal
description: Central American pancake of flour and cornmeal, can be filled with ingredients such as cheese, peppers, or meat.

name: Pequin pepper

name: purslane

name: quince

name: ras el hanout
summary: Arabic originated blend of spices for cooking

name: rutabagas
summary: a root vegetable between a cabbage and turnip

name: salsify

description: Produces edible leafy shoots as well as an edible root.

description: Sweet breads refer to organ meats of beef or veal, often cooked for tenderness and used either in pates or as an ingredient in entrees. They are sometimes poached in milk and served with membranes removed.

name: tagine
summary: A clay pot based stew, often with braised meat
description: Tagine is a cooking vessel used to slow cook food. It can be used on a stove top or in fire pits more traditionally, or covered with burning coals. The origins are north african or middle eastern.

name: taramosalata ταραμοσαλάτα
summary: A greek or turkish cold meze (salad) dip made of cod
description: A greek or turkish cold meze (salad) dip made of cod or sometimes roe. It is used as a spread for bread.

name: turnips
summary: A root vegetable with white bulb and leafy top
description: The leaves can be eaten and may be called rapa.

name: aceitunas
description: olive; the olive is a fruit of the olive tree, native to the mediterranean region. It is rich in oils that are used throughout cooking. When harvested, they are typically green and have a bitter taste. Processes of fermentation or curing are used to remove bitterness and add taste. Common fermenation involves soaking in vinegar, salt, and water, or curing in salt, lye, or fresh water dissolution of the bitter phenolic compounds.

name: acelgas
description: Chard, or swiss chard as its commonly called in the US, is a typical vegetable in mediterranean cooking. It has a consistency similar to celery and is the leafy part of the same vegetable which produces the edible root: beets. There are multiple varieties and colors and depending on the maturity of the leaves, various uses. Young tender leaves may be eaten raw; larger mature leaves can be cooked to softness.

name: achicoria
description: Chicory is a leafy herb or vegetable commonly raw as a salad leaf. It has a nutty, slightly bitter flavor and consistency similar to cabbage. In america, France, and Belgium, it is known as endive. There are various forms and radicchio is a reddish leaf form. Radicchio is commonly served raw or can be grilled with olive oil.

name: aguacate
description: A fruit; actually a berry of the avocado tree.Commonly used in mexican and latin american cooking. Main ingredient in Guacamole. Avocado is high in monounsaturated fats, potassium, and other vitamins. It originates in Central and South America and the word is derived from the Nahuatl (Aztec language) word āhuacatl, meaning "testicle", most likely due to the appearance of the fruit.

name: ahumados
description: Adjective for "smoked", or can be used to describe smoked fish

name: albóndigas
description: meatballs typically served in Spanish cuisine are an appetizer. It is derived from the arabic word "al-bunduq" which refers to hazelnut or other small round object. Albóndigas is thought to have origins from the muslim rule of Spain.

name: alcachofas
description: A thistle plant originating from southern Europe and the mediterranean the part of the artichoke that is edible is the bud of the flower. It is thought to have been cultivated from the wild origins in northern africa. Artichokes can be prepared a number of ways with the tips of the leaves with the thistles are usually cut away, or the leaves are stripped down to the most tender center. It can also be made into a tea.

name: alcaparras
description: Caper is the berry or bud of a spiny bush (Capparis Spinosa) that grows wild in mediterranean regions. It's often pickled or salted.

name: almejas
description: clams, when made with wine and parsley: a la marinera

name: almendras
description: Almonds are the seeds (not actually a nut) of a fruit tree that has cultivation history dating back to the bronze age. It originates in the middle east and is now grown around the world in moderate climates. It is low in carbohydrate and high in monounsaturated fats and can be used as a good flour substitute in gluten free recipes. Almonds are used extensively in sweet and savory applications.

name: anchoas

name: bacalao
summary: Cod, often dried and salted, a popular ingredient
description: Cod fish is salted and dried for storage and long shelf life, but is brought into a light, flaky moist form with rehydration. This ingredient has many uses and its preparation requires that much of the salt must be soaked out before cooking. The cod becomes a light textured, flaky white meat. Taxonomically, cod refers to 3 species based on geography: Pacific, Atlantic, and Greenland. However, in gastronomy, cod is loosely used to describe a number of fish which produces similarly flaky textured meat such as ling cod or rock cod. Can be called "Haddock or Whiting".

name: bacalao a la vizaína
summary: Salt cod served with ham peppers and chilis

description: This dish is raw cod that is salt preserved and has a strong fish/cod flavor.

name: besugo al horno
description: sea bream is a small fish with delicate white flaky meat and skin. It's often sold as dorado or dorade and is a saltwater fish.

name: bizcochos
description: "lady finger" cakes are soft light yellow cakes, lightly sweetened, lightly crisp on the outside and soft inside, often used in many desserts.

name: bocadillos
description: In Spain, it refers to sandwich on a sliced baguette roll, usually with a cold cut like chorizo and moistened with tomato. In Mexico, bocadillo refers to appetizers.

name: bonito

name: butifarra
description: Catalan sausage, also known as Llonganissa in some regions. It is typically a rich pork sausage and may be seasoned with truffle. The dish "butifarra amb seques" is sausage with beans, a Catalan classical dish.

name: cachelada
summary: Pork stew with eggs, tomato, and onion

name: caldereta gallega

name: cangrejos de río

name: chocolate

Xocolātl was often flavored with vanilla and was considered a prized drink and continued to be consumed as a drink primarily into the 1700s. Dutch chocolatiers then created processes to extract cocoa butter to produce the confection we know today as chocolate.

name: churros

name: conejo estofado

It may be finished with hot dry heat like baking, searing, or grilling. The base fluid is typically then reduced down to make a sauce.

name: consomé al jerez
description: A consommé (french origin) is a clarified broth, often used as a base for other soups or dishes. Consommé differs from straight broth in that is is clarified by a process of adding egg white to a broth. The egg white creates foamy scum, binding with the egg white (albumin) all the small particles of vegetable or meat used to flavor the broth. The clear consommé below is poured out.
